problem: Zero-shot 3D scene-graph navigation methods compress visual observations into text-only relation edges, which costs many MLLM queries, irreversibly loses visual evidence, and is limited to a preset vocabulary. Most zero-shot methods also stop at a nearest traversable point after localizing the target, which gives bad final viewpoints (the 'last-mile' problem).
motivation: Real-world navigation needs open-vocabulary generalization and low training cost, so zero-shot methods are attractive, but text-only graphs hurt scene understanding and are expensive to build. The authors observe that 3D-Mem often approaches the target yet fails because the final stop is 0.25-1.0 m away at a poor or occluded viewpoint, so visual evidence and a viewpoint choice both matter.
key_idea: Replace textual relation edges of a 3D scene graph with dynamically assigned images (M3DSG), prune it to a small key subgraph for a VLM, and pick the final navigation viewpoint by a 3D ray-casting visibility score.
insight: Image edges carry information that text relations lose, especially for language and image goals: Node-only 51.8 SR, Concept-Graph 56.2, M3DSG 60.0 on the first-episode GOAT-Bench subset. The largest single gain comes from VVD: without it SR is 33.91 at d=0.25 m and 62.38 at 1.0 m, which shows many failures are last-mile errors, while with VVD it is 51.97. AVU and CLR help only in combination (each alone hurts some goal types), so they are complementary.
method: M3DSG: object-centric graph (nodes with category, 3D position, point cloud, CLIP feature, room) built incrementally from YOLO-World, SAM and CLIP; each edge between nearby objects (distance < 3.5 m) stores the set of RGB-D images where the pair co-occurs, so no VLM query is needed for relations.

Key Subgraph Selection (KSS): Compress the graph to an ID/category adjacency list; Focus by having the VLM pick the top-20 target-relevant objects; Prune with a greedy set-cover over edge images. This gives ~4 images per query and >95% token reduction.
Adaptive Vocabulary Update (AVU): starts from the ScanNet-200 vocabulary; the VLM inspects edge images and proposes novel category words, which are added to the detector vocabulary online.
Closed-Loop Reasoning (CLR): stores past VLM responses as decision memory M_t and feeds it back into the next query (with a task-completion verification step using past observation images).

Visibility-based Viewpoint Decision (VVD): samples K=20 candidate viewpoints at radii 0.5 and 0.75 m around the target centroid at camera height 1.5 m, keeps traversable ones, and scores each by the fraction of target points whose ray to the viewpoint is unoccluded (margin τ=0.05 m) in the scene point cloud. The best-scoring viewpoint becomes the navigation goal.
Reasoning loop: the VLM gets the key subgraph, frontier images (as in 3D-Mem), decision memory and the goal, and returns either a target object or a frontier to explore.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (2024-08-06, frozen) as the main VLM; Qwen-VL-Max as an alternative; YOLO-World, SAM and CLIP as frozen perception models
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose (120° HFOV camera, 1280x1280 images, 512x512 for prompts)
setting.action_space: high-level target or frontier selection by the VLM, then a low-level planner to a chosen viewpoint (VVD) or frontier
setting.privileged: none stated (uses agent pose and depth to build the map)

numbers_note: The main text says '52.0% SPL and 29.6% SPL' (typo). The ablation tables use only the first episode of each scene, so they are not reported as main numbers. The HM3D-ObjNav split is not named in the paper; 'val' is assumed.
results: MSGNav reaches 52.0 SR / 29.6 SPL on GOAT-Bench val-unseen, beating the trained MTU3D (47.2/27.7) and the best zero-shot baseline TANGO (32.1/16.5). On HM3D-ObjNav it gets 74.1 SR / 33.4 SPL versus WMNav 72.2/33.3. On HM3D-OVON val-seen it has higher SPL (27.0) but lower SR (48.3) than MTU3D (55.0).
limitations: Latency of VFMs and VLMs makes inference slow, so real-time deployment is not achieved.
The last-mile problem is only mitigated: VVD gains persist as the success threshold is relaxed.
Evaluated in simulation only; the HM3D-ObjNav SPL gain over WMNav is negligible, and the baseline on GOAT-Bench is a reproduced 3D-Mem.
